RagShortTexts: Milan anchored Lombardy's Po Valley agriculture and commanded Europe's finest armor workshops.

Variants.Content: Center of Lombardy's fertile Po basin, Milan dominated northern Italian road networks. It was Europe's undisputed capital of armor manufacturing, where guild armourers utilized Alpine iron and water-powered trip hammers to fashion tempered mail and transitional plates amidst intense rivalry between the Torriani and Visconti clans.

In the armorers' quarter, watermills drive deafening trip-hammers. Milanese masters understand biomechanics intimately, articulating overlapping plates so seamlessly that harness feels like a second skin.
Going into battle clad in Milanese forged gear doubles a soldier's confidence. Heavy crossbow quarrels deflect off cold-worked iron surfaces with nothing worse than a shower of sparks.
